subject.title: Upgrade 2026.6.8→2026.6.9 corrupts email channel config with spurious groupAllowFrom field

question: Should OpenClaw core doctor refuse `groupAllowFrom` writes when it cannot see a channel plugin schema, or should external plugins get an explicit opt-in migration contract first?
rationale: The bug is real, but the remaining choice is the compatibility boundary for external plugin config repair during upgrade.

options.title: Land Schema-Verified Guard
options.body: Merge the narrow fail-closed guard once normal gates pass, leaving schemaless external channel config untouched by core doctor.

options.title: Add External Opt-In
options.body: Pause the fix and design a plugin doctor/schema capability so external channels can opt into this migration safely.

options.title: Use Broader Protection Only
options.body: Supersede the narrow PR only if broader config-protection work proves the same email/RCS regression behavior and coverage.

recommendation.title: Land Schema-Verified Guard
recommendation.body: Merge the narrow fail-closed guard once normal gates pass, leaving schemaless external channel config untouched by core doctor.

likelyOwner.reason: This account introduced and merged the fallback migration being repaired, so it is the strongest routing signal for the compatibility-boundary choice.
